messages:
neha.s: @channel heads-up: we just received a P1 from Acme Apps — they hit a burst of 5xx (mostly 503, some 504) against our hosted inference endpoint in us-west-2 starting around 2025-12-15T09:12:14Z. They report streaming calls that hang and then the SDK goes into tight retry loops, causing duplicate requests and unexpected billing. Example curl response they sent:

neha.s: ```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "gptx-13b", "prompt": "<long prompt>", "stream": true }

< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 09:12:14 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< {"error":{"message":"service temporarily overloaded"}}
```

neha.s: SDK logs show immediate reconnects and retried streams. Escalating to eng-oncall/runtime.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1245. Priority: P1. Oncall notified.

eng-oncall-bot: Oncall assigned: ryan (eng-runtime). Paging @ryan

marta: can you confirm the SDK version, http/1.1 vs http2, and connection pooling settings? Also do they set Connection: keep-alive or default pooling?

neha.s: customer reports SDK 2.3.1 (node), http2 enabled, default pool. ~60 concurrent streams, avg prompt length ~1200 tokens, p95 latency before failures ~1.5s then jumps. Billing spike lines up with retry bursts.

ryan: on it. first-pass hypothesis: long-lived streaming + http2 multiplexing causes head-of-line queueing at the edge/proxy; when the edge is overloaded it starts returning 503 for new streams. Immediate retries from SDK amplify the load. Can you paste an SDK log snippet with retry timing and request ids?

neha.s: logs:

```
[2025-12-15T09:12:13.451Z] requestId=rid_abc123 status=200 stream=chunked
[2025-12-15T09:12:14.623Z] requestId=rid_def456 status=503 reason="upstream overloaded"
[2025-12-15T09:12:14.624Z] sdk.retry attempt=1 backoff=0ms requestId=rid_def456
[2025-12-15T09:12:14.625Z] requestId=rid_ghi789 status=503 reason="upstream overloaded"
[2025-12-15T09:12:14.626Z] sdk.retry attempt=1 backoff=0ms requestId=rid_ghi789
[2025-12-15T09:12:15.000Z] requestId=rid_abc123 status=200 stream=closed
```

marta: that 0ms backoff is a red flag. SDK should use jittered exponential backoff for 5xx/stream failures. 2.3.1 may have poor defaults for streaming. Also ask eng-infra for edge proxy metrics: active connections, stream counts, GOAWAYs, queued requests, NLB target health.

ryan: repro plan: 1) load test against staging to open ~60 concurrent http2 streaming sessions with long prompts; 2) try client switching to http/1.1 (Connection: close) to compare; 3) force SDK backoff min=200ms + jitter and cap concurrency to 12 per process. I'll run the first test now against a staging pool.

samuel (eng-infra): pulling NLB/edge metrics for the period; will check socket stats, TIME_WAIT, and target response times. Do we do per-customer connection pinning?

marta: we don't pin. Customer reuses a small number of http2 connections with many streams — efficient normally but brittle for long-lived streams.

ryan: staging run results (summary): with 60 concurrent streams p95 token latency rises 1.2s -> 3.8s after ~90s, then edge begins returning 503s at ~4% error rate. Switching clients to Connection: close (http/1.1) drops error rate to ~0.8% but reduces throughput ~15%. Enabling backoff (min 200ms + jitter) and reducing concurrency to 12 brings error rate to ~0.2% and system remains stable.

ryan: captured edge logs showing repeated HTTP/2 GOAWAYs:

```
[edge] 2025-12-15T09:13:45Z level=warn event=goaway reason="stream limit exceeded" active_streams=102
[edge] 2025-12-15T09:13:46Z level=info event=queue_len value=240
[edge] 2025-12-15T09:13:46Z level=error event=upstream_503 count=18
```

marta: "stream limit exceeded" points to our http2 stream cap + long TTFB for some streams causing backlog. Could be kernel socket backlog too. Loop in eng-infra to check kernel/tcp backlog and NLB overflow.

samuel: NLB target health shows spikes in response time coincident with the customer's test. Also see increase in TIME_WAIT sockets from connections not being reused cleanly. No per-customer pinning. Need to know SDK sharing model for http2 connections (single shared conn vs many).

marta: customer uses default pooling so they reuse a few http2 connections with many streams.

ryan: working hypothesis (root cause): edge http2 stream limit + many long-lived streams caused queue growth at the edge. Edge began rejecting new streams with 503/504 and issuing GOAWAYs; client SDK immediate retries (0ms backoff) created additional attempts, amplifying load and causing duplicate billing. Short-term mitigation: advise customer to configure SDK exponential backoff with min 200ms + jitter, reduce per-process concurrency to ~10-12, and consider disabling http2 multiplexing for critical pipelines. Medium-term: infra will raise http2 stream caps and kernel backlog; runtime will add 429/backpressure hints rather than immediate 503s. Long-term: implement server-side slow-stream detection and rate-limit/backpressure hints and publish safety defaults in SDK 2.4.0.

neha.s: customer asks for an external update and ETA for mitigations. Drafted message: 

"Hi — thanks for the report and the logs. We identified that a combination of long-lived streaming requests and http2 connection multiplexing caused temporary queuing at our edge leading to 503s. Workarounds you can apply immediately: (1) configure your SDK to use exponential backoff with min 200ms and jitter; (2) reduce concurrent streams per process to ~10–12; (3) if you're using http2 multiplexing, try switching to http/1.1 (Connection: close) for critical pipelines while we roll a fix. We're rolling edge mitigations now (raising stream caps and adding queue backpressure logic). We'll follow up with a timeline and a postmortem. Sorry for the disruption — we understand the billing and reliability impact and will prioritize a fix."

neha.s: customer approved sending that. Please include ETAs when we have them.

ryan: mitigation ETA summary: infra will increase http2 stream limit and kernel backlog in us-west-2 edge nodes tonight (rolling, ETA ~3 hours); runtime change to return 429 backpressure hints for queued streams (ETA 24–36 hours); SDK safety defaults (jittered exponential backoff) in 2.4.0 (ETA ~48 hours). I'll post task updates here.

samuel (eng-infra): rolling kernel backlog + stream cap changes to 20% of edge nodes now; watch window 30m. Early telemetry: queued requests down ~38% and 5xx down ~60% on updated nodes. Continuing rollout.

support-bot: status change: customer notified with workaround; mitigation rollout started. INC-2025-1245 -> Monitoring.

neha.s: thanks all. Action items: Marta to create KB with recommended SDK settings and repro notes for CSEs; Ryan to update when each mitigation completes; Samuel to finish edge roll and post metrics. I'll keep the customer updated and post the postmortem when ready.

marta: I'll create the KB/playbook: 1) ask SDK version & concurrency; 2) request ids + logs; 3) temp fixes (backoff, concurrency, http1.1) + drafted message; 4) cost explanation re: duplicate billing and how to mitigate. Will link here when done.

ryan: kernel backlog roll completed to 100% of nodes at 2025-12-15T12:05Z. System-wide 5xx down ~72% compared to peak window. Proceeding with runtime changes next.

neha.s: update customer with mitigation progress and ETA for runtime change tonight. Will follow up with postmortem.

support-bot: Incident INC-2025-1245: last update 2025-12-15T12:45:20Z.
